title: Pipeline-span instrumentation for prefill/decode GPU ranges and per-kernel timing
creator: Ravi Kaur
description: Goal: Add lightweight, production-safe instrumentation that exposes distinct prefill vs decode GPU ranges and per-kernel timing/metadata so Console and Debug traces can answer: which kernels dominate latency for short vs long sequences, where does KV/prefix cache effect show up, and how scheduling choices change decode tail latency. Scope: instrument runtime hot paths to emit GPU range markers (NVTX or equivalent) and host trace spans for: prefill stage (embedding, attention precomputes, KV write), decode stage (attention+FFN kernels, KV read), and the kernel scheduler/dispatcher. Capture per-kernel metrics: wall-clock time, launch-to-completion, SM occupancy estimate, bytes moved, and invocation count. Implementation must be behind a runtime flag and sampling rate to keep overhead <2% p99 for typical workloads. Deliverables: 1) Instrumentation library additions + feature flag, 2) mapping table of kernel symbol -> logical span names (e.g., ATTN_PREFILL, ATTENTION_DECODE, KV_WRITE), 3) Console integrations: new trace view with stacked prefill/decode bars and per-kernel breakdown, 4) dashboards for decode vs prefill token time percentiles by model and hardware, 5) docs and a short runbook for interpreting traces. Trade-offs: NVTX provides best GPU-side granularity but requires GPU drivers and increases overhead; host-only spans are cheaper but miss kernel overlap. We will implement both and prefer NVTX when available. Acceptance criteria: - NVTX/host spans emitted under feature flag with configurable sampling - Trace contains separate prefill and decode stacks visible in Console for at least 3 model families (gpt-like, long-context, and quantized variants) - Per-kernel timing visible in trace and aggregated in perf dashboards with 50/95/99 percentiles by route/model - End-to-end p99 latency regressions <=2% when instrumentation is enabled at sampling=0.1% - Documented mapping and example investigations (confluence + example traces) Links: spike notes + approach: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/742391/GPU+profiling+plan, PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3762
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: spike completed by Ravi. Verified NVTX gives per-kernel ranges on CUDA 12+ and roctx on ROCm. Chose design to emit both NVTX and a host-level trace span for portability.

2026-02-24 - Implementation note: kernel symbol demangling added to runtime symbol table to map low-level cuLaunchKernel names to logical spans. Prototype shows ATTENTION kernel group accounts for ~65% of decode token time in small-batch tests.

2026-03-01 - PR opened: runtime instrumentation + feature flag (pr:3762). Initial reviewers: Marisol (performance), Jonah (observability). Comments: require sampling knobs and opt-out env var; add CI microbench to measure overhead.

2026-03-04 - Microbench results: with sampling at 0.1% overhead measured at p50 +0.1%, p99 +1.3% in end-to-end echo benchmark on a4 instance. Need to trim NVTX payloads to avoid driver-side string copies; switched to integer tag IDs.

2026-03-07 - Design feedback from Console team (Priya): prefer aggregated per-kernel metrics sent periodically instead of per-request verbose traces to avoid high cardinality in ingestion. Approach: retain full traces for sampled requests and emit aggregated rollups every minute (model, kernel_group, avg_time, count).

2026-03-10 - Next: address Console ingestion format (spec doc in PR), add dashboard queries, and run a canary on dedicated infra with production traffic. Follow-ups: support kernel-level counters for quantized kernels, and add mapping for patched/custom fused kernels used by inference-optimizer.
